name: blackbody_band_fraction
title: Blackbody band fraction f_1_2 (Planck law integral)
summary: Fraction of the blackbody emissive power emitted between two wavelengths lambda_1 and lambda_2 at the absolute temperature T: the Planck spectral emissive power is integrated with the EES INTEGRAL function (step 0.01 um) and divided by sigma#*T^4. As in the original EES example, T is in K and lambda in um.

origin.notes: Example of the F-Chart Software EES example set (plain-text MIT mirror: https://github.com/EES-Community/ees-examples, uncategorized/blackbody.ees).

verification.summary: Compared with the solution stored in the source EES file: 7 common variables, 0 differ (rtol=0.001), largest deviation 1.35e-4 on E_b (Stefan-Boltzmann constant: CoolSolve sigma# is the CODATA value, the stored value implies 5.66961e-8); f_1_2 agrees to 4.9e-6. The transcribed constants C1/C2 reproduce all 100 rows of the stored parametric table (Planck sweep).
verification.reference: EES stored solution of ~/Nextcloud/thermo_models/EES_library/Blackbody.EES (ees_variables.csv) and its stored parametric table (100 rows of E_lambda_b at T = 5000 K)
verification.notes: compare_solution.py --all: 7 common variables, 0 differ (rtol=0.001); only in CoolSolve: 3 (C1, C2, sigma#, constants of the transcription). The triage check f_1_2 = 0.3700 at T = 5000 K between 0.3 and 0.7 um is reproduced (0.370047 vs 0.370049 stored).
